English
On World COPD Day, I’m sharing this conversation with LA NACIÓN about a disease that remains far too invisible: more than 70% of people with COPD have not been diagnosed.
Early diagnosis can change lives. Breathing is a right, not a privilege.

Thank you to Gabriela Navarra Camerucci and LA NACIÓN for helping bring lung health into the public conversation.

#WorldCOPDDay #COPD #LungHealth #BreathingIsARight

text:
A new study in @BMJOpen_Resp suggests that early-life exposure to #airpollution is linked to poorer lung function 🫁 in childhood, and that the difference persists into adolescence.

Researchers from the University of Copenhagen followed 846 mother-child pairs in the Danish COPSAC2000 and COPSAC2010 cohorts. They modelled exposure to PM2.5 and NO₂ during #pregnancy and the first year of life, and measured lung function from age 3 to 18. Each extra 2 µg/m³ of PM2.5 during pregnancy was associated with nearly 2% lower #lung capacity at age six, and higher exposure was linked to slower lung development through childhood and adolescence.

These effects showed up at relatively low levels. The average annual PM2.5 in the study was 9.6 µg/m³, compared with the @WHO guideline of 5 µg/m³. A

For one child the difference is small, but across a population even small shifts matter for #health. Protecting pregnant women and young children from polluted air is an early investment in lifelong lung health.

https://t.co/QCygpZ4c3J
author_headline: Technical Officer, @WHO Department of #NCDs and #mentalhealth. UN NCD Task Force Secretariat. Support countries achieve #health related #SDGs. PhD MPH MD.

triage.reason: WHO official sharing new BMJ Open Respiratory study on early-life air pollution.

text:
Dr Kavindhran Velen, Chief Scientific Officer, The Union, delivers the opening statement during the Spotlight Session on From TB to Lung Health: Building Integrated Primary Care Models for Earlier Detection at the #UnionConf2026 in Rio de Janeiro.

“Integration must go beyond expanding services - it must deliver better outcomes for people without compromising the strengths of the TB programme. This requires three essentials: protecting TB programme performance through timely diagnosis and treatment, adequately resourcing primary healthcare to deliver integrated services, and demonstrating tangible benefits for patients.

Ultimately, success must be measured not only by sustained TB outcomes, but also by improved health, better access to care, fewer repeat visits and reduced costs for patients.”

#UnionConf2026
author_name: International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (The Union)

triage.reason: Union CSO statement on integrating TB and lung health care

text:
🚨 Place healthcare workers at the centre of any new climate and health initiative 

That’s the message from a coalition of 18 leading health professional organisations – including ERS – who have called on the #COP31 Presidency to place healthcare workers at the centre of its new climate and health initiative.

Alongside its partners in the coalition, ERS urges the creation of a dedicated health workforce pillar within the Antalya Initiative for Resilient Health Systems (AIR) – a new drive to strengthen countries’ ability to prepare for, respond to, and adapt to climate-related health threats under the COP31 Türkiye Action Agenda.

Read more about the initiative: https://lnkd.in/eTfs3vzR

triage.reason: ERS coalition advocacy on health workforce in COP31 initiative
